land.text: Attica and Boeotia, conquered by Boniface of Montferrat in November 1204 and granted to Othon de la Roche ('To Othon de la Roche, he gave Athens')

predecessors.note: Othon page: the grant is late 1204; the Duchy page infobox gives 'Fourth Crusade: 1204' and 'Duchy established: 1205'. The state is drawn from 1205.

land.text: Athens and Thebes, surrendered to the Catalan Company after Halmyros (15 March 1311); the Duchy's land from 1311, which Cliopatria's Catalan Company row picks up only in 1314

successors.note: The Duchy page treats the Catalan period (1311-1388) as the same Duchy under a new dynasty and runs it to 1458; Cliopatria and this batch's split give the Catalan period to the catalan-company row. See notes.

capitals.name: Athens
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital(s): Athens, Thebes'; the Othon page says Athens 'remained his residence, with his castle on the Acropolis'.

capitals.name: Thebes (Thiva)
capitals.note: Co-capital: 'Thebes became his capital and economic centre because of its silk industry'; Othon held Thebes 'by around 1211'. The two seats overlap; Athens is the first.

correction.text: shape unchanged (Attica and Boeotia, 26 cells), but it holds from 1205, the year the Duchy page's infobox gives for the founding; Thebes itself was Albertino of Canossa's until Emperor Henry took it on 8 May 1209 and is Othon's only 'by around 1211'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: infobox 'Fourth Crusade: 1204', 'Duchy established: 1205'; Cliopatria starts 1206. The page gives no area (so no infobox comparison); the shape is the 'Attic peninsula as well as Boeotia' the page names. The Argolid is not in this shape and stays out (see the 1216 verdict).

correction.text: the Attica-and-Boeotia shape of 1206 without the Argolid: Argos and Nauplia were 'a fief' granted by Geoffrey I of Villehardouin, prince of Achaea, to Othon de la Roche in 1212 and are drawn by the Achaea dossier as its vassal land held by the dukes of Athens

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria adds the Argolid (bbox south to 37.45 N) from 1216 to 1271. The page says Acrocorinth fell in 1210, then Nauplia, 'then Argos in 1212', granted 'as a fief' to Otto; the lordship was a fief of Achaea although 'its holders were the Dukes of Athens'. To avoid drawing it twice (the Achaea dossier has it as vassal_start duchy-of-athens 1212 to vassal_end 1388) the Argolid is removed from the Duchy. If the orchestrator prefers the dukes' personal union drawn as Athens, restore the Cliopatria shape.

correction.text: the 1206 shape (Attica and Boeotia) without the Argolid, as for 1216-1235

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as 1216 with one more northern cell (8,834 against 8,687 km2); the pages opened date no change in 1236 (Thessalonica fell in 1224 and the Empire of Thessalonica row starts in 1236, which explains nothing on the Duchy's own land). The Argolid is removed as for 1216.

correction.text: the 1206 shape (Attica and Boeotia) without the Argolid

keyframe_review.note: Same as the 1216 shape. Guy I held the Argolid as William II's feudatory from 1251 (Otto II sold him the Greek possessions in April 1251); the pages open no territorial change in 1258 or 1259: Karydi ended the war with Guy's submission, and the 1262 peace 'restored the status quo ante bellum' (Euboeote page).

8,192 km2, the Attica-and-Boeotia core without the Argolid. The Lordship page records no transfer of Argos and Nauplia in 1263-1278 (they stay with the dukes as fief of Achaea), so the Argolid's absence is right for the Duchy and its presence in Achaea's shape is the vassal tint. No territorial event is dated for 1272 in the pages opened; the 1267 Treaties of Viterbo ('the Duchy recognized the suzerainty of Charles I of Sicily') change the overlord, not the land.

8,242 km2: the same core with one cell more at the west edge (lon 22.39). The pages opened date no change in 1279; Cliopatria's neighbour list gives Anjou-Sicily as the Duchy's neighbour for 1279-1293 (Achaea merged into the Angevin row). Unverified beyond the core: page budget.

correction.text: shape unchanged but it ends in March 1311: after the Battle of Halmyros (15 March 1311) 'Athens was surrendered to the victors by Walter's widow, Joanna of Châtillon' and the land is the Catalan Company's; Cliopatria's Catalan Company row begins only in 1314

keyframe_review.note: Years only. Shape 1305-1313 is drawn Frankish for two years too long (1311-1313): the catalan-company dossier should carry this same shape from 1311. 'only the lordship of Argos and Nauplia in the Peloponnese remained in the hands of Brienne loyalists' (Achaea's fief, not in this shape).

region.text: Attica and Boeotia, 'the Attic peninsula as well as Boeotia'

ledger.note: 1205: Othon de la Roche establishes the Lordship of Athens, with Thebes. Infobox 'Duchy established: 1205'; the Othon page: Boniface of Montferrat 'conquered Thessaly, Boeotia, and Attica in November 1204 and granted them to his commanders', 'To Othon de la Roche, he gave Athens'. Othon took the title Megaskyr ('Grand Lord') and proclaimed himself 'Lord of Athens'; the page gives the peninsula and Boeotia, not a boundary. Originally a vassal of the Kingdom of Thessalonica.

region.text: Thebes, Albertino of Canossa's until Henry took it on 8 May 1209

ledger.note: c. 1211: Othon holds Thebes. Emperor Henry took Thebes from Albertino of Canossa on 8 May 1209; 'it is unclear whether Henry then gave Thebes to Othon in 1209 or whether it was not granted until before 1211' and the lead has Othon acquiring it 'by around 1211'. Thebes became 'his capital and economic centre'. The year is the page's approximation; the Cliopatria shape includes Thebes from 1206.

region.text: Attica and Boeotia, raided by William of Villehardouin; Karydi pass on the Megara-Thebes road; Thebes besieged

ledger.note: 1258: Achaean army crosses the Isthmus into Attica and Boeotia. Villehardouin 'raided Attica' (undated) and his army 'crossed the Isthmus of Corinth and defeated the coalition at the pass of Mount Karydi, on the road from Megara to Thebes'; Guy I and the barons fled to the citadel of Thebes. Guy joined the Lombard-Venetian camp 'from summer 1256' (war from 1256), but the first campaign on the Duchy's own ground the page dates is 1258; the Achaea dossier starts the contest in 1256.

1258: Karydi ends the war on the Athenian front. 'Their defeat at the Battle of Karydi in May/June 1258 effectively brought the war to an end in an Achaean victory'; Villehardouin withdrew from Thebes on Guy's pledge to appear before the High Court at Nikli; no land changed hands. Treaty only in 1262 (status quo ante bellum).

1260: Guy I is Duke of Athens. After the war Guy went to France in 1259 and 'Louis not only pardoned him, but awarded him the title of duke'; the Duchy page says 'the title did not become official until 1260'. The Lordship of Athens becomes the Duchy; same state, same colour.

1309: the Brienne succeed the de la Roche. 'On 5 October 1308, the last de la Roche Duke of Athens, Guy II, died childless'; 'in mid-1309, the High Court (feudal council) of Achaea chose his cousin' Walter V of Brienne. A dynasty change within the same state (the Duchy page gives Walter 1308-1311).

region.text: Athens and Thebes, Attica and Boeotia

ledger.note: 1311: the Duchy falls at Halmyros. On 15 March 1311 Walter V of Brienne and 'almost the entire knighthood of his realm' fall to the Catalan Company he had hired and refused to pay; 'Finally, Athens was surrendered to the victors by Walter's widow, Joanna of Châtillon'. Thebes plundered. Only Argos and Nauplia (Achaea's fief) stay with the Brienne. The Catalans recognise Frederick of Sicily in 1312 (Duchy page). The Duchy page keeps the name for the Catalan, Acciaioli and Venetian periods to 1456/1458.

wars.name: War of the Euboeote Succession

zones.text: Attica and Boeotia: Villehardouin raided Attica, beat the coalition at Karydi on the Megara-Thebes road and prepared to besiege Thebes

wars.outcome: Achaean victory at Karydi (May/June 1258); Guy I submitted and was pardoned by Louis IX, who made him duke; the 1262 treaty restored the status quo ante bellum.
wars.note: Euboea (Negroponte) was the cause and the main theatre, not Athenian land. The Athens side starts with Guy's entry in summer 1256, but the page dates ground contested in the Duchy only in 1258, hence the ledger's contest_start in 1258.

wars.name: Catalan Company conquest of Athens (Battle of Halmyros)

zones.text: Athens and Thebes, surrendered after the battle of 15 March 1311

wars.outcome: Catalan victory at Halmyros on 15 March 1311; Walter V killed; Athens surrendered by his widow; the Catalans took the Duchy except Argos and Nauplia.
wars.note: The Catalans entered Thessaly in early 1309 and were hired by Walter for six months against the Greeks; no contest_start in the ledger because the Duchy's land changed hands in one stroke after the battle, which was fought at Halmyros in southern Thessaly, not on Duchy ground.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary: the Duchy is 'the Attic peninsula as well as Boeotia'. The Isthmus pass at Megara and the Euripus are natural limits but no treaty or survey fixes them. The Argolid fief (not drawn as Duchy land) is the one exception whose extent the sources name (Argos and Nauplia).

notes: Within the 5-page budget; rulers key omitted because no opened page lists the de la Roche dukes after Othon (the Duchy page's list starts with Walter V of Brienne 1308; the 'List of dukes of Athens' was not opened). SPLIT AT 1311: Wikipedia's 'Duchy of Athens' runs 1205-1458 (Catalan 1311-1388, Acciaioli 1388-1458, Venetian podestas 1395-1402); Cliopatria's Duchy of Athens row ends 1313 and its Catalan Company row begins 1314, and the catalan-company slug belongs to batch eu-05-e. This dossier therefore ends at Halmyros (15 March 1311) with the catalan-company dossier as successor. If the orchestrator treats the Catalan duchy as the same state (rule 2: a dynasty change is a rename), merge catalan-company into this dossier. Either way Cliopatria lacks the Acciaioli Duchy of Athens (1388-1458, Nerio Acciaioli took Athens in 1388; Corinth held from 1371) and the 1311-1313 years of the Frankish shape need the Catalan dossier to start in 1311. ARGOLID: Cliopatria draws Argos and Nauplia with Athens in 1216-1271 and with Achaea otherwise; the Lordship page makes them a fief of Achaea 'although its holders were the Dukes of Athens' (1212-1388, retained by the Brienne after 1311). The Achaea dossier already records the Argolid as vassal land of Achaea, so this dossier removes it from the Duchy (keyframes 1216, 1236, 1241) and records no gain for it; the viewer caption for 1212 is Achaea's. A separate state 'Lordship of Argos and Nauplia' (1212-1388) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier. SUZERAINTY (no ledger type exists for becoming a vassal; the suzerain's dossier carries the vassal_start with duchy-of-athens as counterpart): Kingdom of Thessalonica (original suzerain, to 1224; Othon 'stayed loyal to King Demetrius of Thessalonica until the Kingdom of Thessalonica ended in 1224'), Latin Empire (the latin-empire dossier has vassal_start 1209 at Ravennika, but the Othon page says Longnon holds that Othon 'never recognised Henry as his direct overlord': disagreement), Principality of Achaea (claimed suzerainty after 1224; Guy a feudatory of William II for Argos and Nauplia), Charles I of Sicily (after the 1267 Treaties of Viterbo), Frederick of Sicily (1312, under the Catalans). Othon also gave Livadeia to the pope in 1214 and received it back as a fief (Othon page). TITLE: Othon was Megaskyr; 'dux' appears in a July 1208 papal letter and the duke title is traditionally Louis IX's gift to Guy I (c. 1259/1260): the rename event of 1260 follows the Duchy page ('did not become official until 1260'). DATES NOT SETTLED: the founding year (late 1204 grant, 1205 in the infobox); the date Thebes came to Othon (1209 to 'around 1211'); Cliopatria's small shape changes in 1236, 1241, 1272 and 1279 (one or two cells) are explained by no opened page. Region names: Attica, Boeotia and Thebes all resolve; no gazetteer names needed.
